 Tulane battles Tulsa in the Green Wave's homecoming game today. Doug Joubert | Share on Facebook Share on X Add us as a preferred source Tulane RB Johnnie Daniels celebrates TD | Corey Hughes With the possibility of making their fifth straight American Conference championship game this year still not completely out of reach (they'd need a lot help along the way to get there), the Tulane football team has made every game from here on out a must win situation. Standing 4-4 on the year, 2-2 in league play, the Green Wave entertain Tulsa this morning at Yulman Stadium. The Golden Hurricane are also 4-4 on the season, but 1-3 in the American. Kickoff is set for 11:00 a.m. CT.

 Key #1: Run the Ball REALLY Well
--> Key #1: Run the Ball REALLY Well
 Tulane RB Johnnie Daniels finds a seam | Corey Hughes Though this Tulsa defense is good, they are below the middle of the defensive pack in the American. They can just as easily give up a big run as much as a big pass. However, the key for this Tulane offense is to do something all game long they've only been able to do in spurts: run the ball, and run it really well.

 The Wave has the stable of running backs to do it, and this young offensive line seems to be jelling. Use Johnnie Daniels, Mo Turner, Jaylin Lucas, DJ Dugar, and throw in a healthy dose of a healthy Jamauri McClure. Then your freshman quarterback can pick apart this Golden Hurricane defense.

 #3: Take Care of (and Take Away) the Ball

Add to that their 7-interceptions, and you have a turnover producing machine. As coach Will Hall and his coaches have reminded the team since the Spring: Rub the nipple, which means to hold the football against your chest tightly, so much so that you can feel the ball through your pads.

 Add us as a preferred source on Google Follow Published 4 hours ago DOUG JOUBERT Doug has covered a gamut of sporting events in his fifty-plus years in the field. He started doing sideline reporting for Louisiana Tech football games for the student radio station. Doug was Sports Director for KNOE-AM/FM in Monroe in the mid-80s, winning numerous awards from the Louisiana Sports Writers Association for Best Sportscast and Best Play-by-Play. High school play-by-play for teams in Monroe, Natchitoches, New Orleans, and Thibodaux, LA dot his resume. He did college play-by-play for Northwestern State University in Natchitoches for nine years. Then, moving to the Crescent City, Doug did television PBP of Tulane games and even filled in for legendary Tulane broadcaster, Ken Berthelot in the only game Kenny ever missed while doing the Green Wave games.
His father was an alumnus of Tulane in the 1940s, so Doug has attended Tulane football games in old Tulane Stadium, the Superdome, and Yulman. He was one of the 86,000 plus on December 1, 1973, sitting in the North End Zone to seeTulane shutout the LSU Tigers, 14-0. He was there when the Posse ruled Fogelman and in Turchin when the Wave made it to the World Series. He currently is the public address voice of the Tulane baseball team.
